Marks: 50                                                                                                      Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1A)               In a signal processing application, two equal-length vectors A and B represent input and weight   (4)  
  values of a digital filter. Each vector contains N elements, and the dot product of these vectors  
  determines the filter output. Develop a CISC-style assembly program to compute the dot product of  
  vectors A and B and store the result in memory location DOTPROD. Describe the sequence of  
  operations required through suitable codes and explanations.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Create"  
  
1B)               Represent the following numbers in 5-bit 2's complement form, perform the operation mentioned            (3)  
  and state whether overflow occurs or not in each case.  
  i) Add +9 and +12  
  ii) Add -8 and -9  
  Subtract -5 from +10  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
1C)               Implement a three-input XOR gate using 4-to-1 multiplexer with a neat diagram.                           (3)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
2A)               Design a sequential circuit with two JK flip-flops A and B and two inputs E and F. If E = 0, the circuit (5)  
  remains in the same state regardless of the value of F. When E = 1 and F = 1, the circuit goes  
  through the state transitions from 00 to 01, to 10, to 11, back to 00, and repeats. When E = 1 and F  
  = 0, the circuit goes through the state transitions from 00 to 11, to 10, to 01, back to 00, and  
  repeats.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Create"  
  
2B)               Design a 3-bit synchronous binary up-counter using T flip-flops. Draw the logic diagram.                 (3)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Create"

  memory contains 8192 blocks, each consisting of 256 words.  
  i) How many bits are there in the main memory address?  
  ii) How many bits are there in each of the TAG, SET, and WORD fields?  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"

  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Evaluate"  
  
4B)   Perform the addition of the following two 32-bit IEEE 754 single-precision floating-point numbers      (3)  
  and represent the result in IEEE 754 format.  
  $$i) A = 0 10000010 10100000000000000000000$$  
  $$ii) B = 0 10000001 11000000000000000000000$$  
  Show all the steps including conversion to decimal, exponent alignment, addition, normalization,  
  and final binary representation.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
4C)   Apply the concept of microprogramming to explain how a control unit generates control signals          (3)  
  during instruction execution, using a suitable diagram.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"
